text:
alex: Hey team — Customer-ops on a call reporting a spike of 429s from APAC this morning. They say traffic kept going but latency jumped and a lot of requests got routed to US and then started failing. Can someone help triage?

customer-ops: yep — we saw ~30% of requests that normally land in ap-southeast-1 get routed to us-east-1. After that a subset returned 429, another subset 401s for the same API key, and a few 504s. It started ~08:03 UTC and lasted ~6m. No config changes from our side.

jia: grabbing logs now. Do we have the regional capacity alert for APAC?

sre-oncall: We had a capacity pressure alert for ap-southeast-1 at 08:01 UTC — autoscaler hit burst limit and refused more GPUs for ~4m. Routing policy should overflow to next region but keep within per-customer quota.

kevin: Important detail: overflow routing will send to a fallback region, but we also enforce the customer's per-region soft quota on the destination for a short window. If the dest region's quota is hit, we throttle with 429. If auth tokens are used across regions, a mis-synced KMS TTL can cause 401s when keys rotate during failover.

alex: customer says their key is the same and they didn't rotate. Could KMS TTL cause transient 401s during cross-region hops?

jia: yes — our private deployments use short-lived session tokens for routing. In hosted mode we sign tokens that carry a region field; failover rewrites that. If a token is validated by an old signing key on the destination, you'll briefly get 401 until KV metadata synchronizes (<1m normally).

customer-ops: logs attached from their client: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-..." https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate``` Response snippets: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Region: ap-southeast-1
Retry-After: 2``` then later ```HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
X-Region: us-east-1
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"redwood\"```

sre-oncall: Can you paste the full edge-id header? That helps track routing path.

customer-ops: edge-id: edg-AP-SOUTHEAST-1-3b9f. We also have client IPs if needed.

kevin: Thanks. Matching that to traces — I see the request hit the ap-southeast edge, then proxy sent an Overflow -> us-east-1 policy at 08:02:13 UTC. On the destination, worker queue was near saturation; the token cache showed a 15s delay on key propagation due to GC on the auth service which we had a benign spike on. That explains the 401s. The 429s are a mix: some from the source region hitting regional per-customer burst limit, others from the destination enforcing its own soft quota while under load.

jia: For mitigation, we can: 1) increase APAC burst top-up (short-term) 2) temporarily disable cross-region routing for this customer to avoid auth edge cases 3) enable queued fallback with immediate 503-style hold rather than redirecting. Which does customer want?

customer-ops: prefer not to disable cross-region routing — their UX needs resiliency. Can we do (1) and reduce the TTL for auth key sync to avoid future 401s?

alex: We can bump the burst credits for that customer in ap-southeast-1 for 10 minutes (manual top-up) and flip auth-sync to fast-sync (down to ~2s) for hosted customers for the next 30m. Do we have a runbook?

sre-oncall: Runbook steps: 
- cmd: `rbctl customers topup --id cust-42 --region ap-southeast-1 --credits 2000 --duration 600`
- cmd: `authctl sync-policy set --fast-sync true --ttl 2 --scope hosted --duration 1800`
- monitor: `alerts region.ap-southeast.capacity` and `auth.sync.latency`

kevin: Also add a temporary safeguard: for next 15m, change fallback policy for cust-42 from direct overflow to queued retry with exponential backoff so we won't hit dest quotas. `routingctl policy set --customer cust-42 --fallback queued-retry --max-retries 3`

customer-ops: doing the topup now. Will report back if 429s stop.

(15m later) customer-ops: update — after the top-up and fast-sync we saw the 429/401 spike drop to baseline. We still saw a couple of 504s during a short GC pause but total error rate returned to normal within ~8m.

alex: Good. Notes for postmortem: add an item to improve auth key propagation under GC, and consider a local edge-level token cache for cross-region validation to avoid 401s on failover. Also clarify routing docs: overflow can hit destination quotas and that may surface as 429s even though source showed capacity pressure.

jia: I'll create a short KB for support explaining: cause = regional capacity + overflow routing + auth sync lag -> symptoms = cross-region 429s and transient 401s -> mitigations = top-up/burst, queued-fallback, fast auth-sync.

kevin: Also add A/B for behavior: queued-fallback preserves ordering but increases latency; overflow reduces latency but risks hitting dest quotas. Useful for customers to pick.

support-bot: Incident annotated: ticket #INC-2026 created, runbook executed, indicators back to normal. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open for a day in case customer sees recurrence.
